title: 3Dtrees: From LiDAR point clouds to individual trees
questions: How can LiDAR describe the three-dimensional structure of a forest?
How can individual trees be identified in a point cloud?
How can segmentation results be inspected in Galaxy?
objectives: Explain what a LiDAR point cloud represents
Standardize and prepare one LAS file for tree segmentation
Distinguish vegetation/non-vegetation classes from individual-tree identifiers
Inspect tree predictions and identify obvious visual problems
key_points: LiDAR records the 3D structure of vegetation and terrain
SegmentAnyTree separates vegetation from non-vegetation points and assigns an ID to each predicted tree
Visual inspection can reveal obvious problems but is not a quantitative accuracy assessment

quiz.title: What can the overview tell you?

questions.title: Which overview image is best for spotting gaps in the canopy?
answers: The top view
The section (side) view
Neither of them

questions.title: Which overview image shows how the vegetation is layered above the ground?
answers: The top view
The section (side) view
Neither of them

questions.title: In which close-up do you expect individual trees to be harder to separate?
answers: Close-up A: taller crowns with gaps between them
Close-up B: lower crowns that touch each other
questions.correct: Close-up B: lower crowns that touch each other

questions.title: Which observations support a plausible segmentation? Select all that apply.
answers: Most instance colours follow recognisable tree crowns rather than scattered patches.
Neighbouring, visibly separate crowns usually have different colours.
Visible ground points are mostly in the non-vegetation class of PredSemantic_SAT.
Many crowns are cut exactly along straight processing boundaries.
One colour spans many unrelated crowns.
correct: Most instance colours follow recognisable tree crowns rather than scattered patches.
Neighbouring, visibly separate crowns usually have different colours.
Visible ground points are mostly in the non-vegetation class of PredSemantic_SAT.

questions.title: Why is this only a visual check and not an accuracy assessment? Select all that apply.
answers: A result can look plausible and still contain missed, merged or split trees.
We did not compare the predictions with independently labelled reference trees.
Measuring accuracy needs reference labels and a method to compare them with predictions.
Potree proves that every displayed tree is correct.
correct: A result can look plausible and still contain missed, merged or split trees.
We did not compare the predictions with independently labelled reference trees.
Measuring accuracy needs reference labels and a method to compare them with predictions.

questions.title: Two neighbouring crowns are both predicted as vegetation but have different PredInstance_SAT values. What does that mean?
answers: They have the same class (vegetation) but are two different individual trees.
They are the same tree, split into two classes.
One of them is ground and the other is vegetation.
They belong to different tree species.
questions.correct: They have the same class (vegetation) but are two different individual trees.

questions.title: Which analyses need the individual-tree instances (PredInstance_SAT)? Select all that apply.
answers: Predicting the species of each tree
Measuring the height of each tree
Counting the trees in the survey area
Mapping where there is vegetation at all
correct: Predicting the species of each tree
Measuring the height of each tree
Counting the trees in the survey area

questions.title: Which statements about the Standardization tool are correct? Select all that apply.
answers: It checks file information and prepares a consistent format for the next tools.
It creates a summary and a footprint of the input.
It assigns every tree a unique identifier.
It proves that later segmentation results are accurate.
It turns unrelated flight areas into one continuous survey.
correct: It checks file information and prepares a consistent format for the next tools.
It creates a summary and a footprint of the input.

questions.title: Why is a buffer useful when a tree crosses a processing boundary?
answers: It gives the model points from beyond the tile edge, so trees near the edge keep their context.
It removes duplicate trees from the result.
It reduces the number of points to process.
It guarantees that every tree is completely inside one tile.
questions.correct: It gives the model points from beyond the tile edge, so trees near the edge keep their context.

questions.title: What happens when you make the buffer wider? Select all that apply.
answers: The model gets more context around trees near the tile edges.
More points are repeated in neighbouring tiles, so processing takes longer.
The same tree is more likely to be predicted in neighbouring tiles.
The predictions become correct everywhere.
correct: The model gets more context around trees near the tile edges.
More points are repeated in neighbouring tiles, so processing takes longer.
The same tree is more likely to be predicted in neighbouring tiles.
